significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, for successful encoded jailbreaks, “decoding happens in later layers, after the refusal decision has been made,” an ordering law between two measurable internal events, plus the causal mechanism that a later refusal check restores refusal; it therefore establishes both the jailbreak phenomenon and a timing-based mechanism. This would constrain predictions across encoding variants—attacks should succeed when decoded-intent emergence lags refusal commitment and should weaken when that order reverses—rather than merely showing that a refusal direction exists; CipherChat (Yuan et al., 2024) documents cipher-mediated safety failure, while Arditi et al. (2024), “Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction,” shows why locating refusal computation is operationally consequential. Verified-true and verified-false are distinguishable: a negative result showing that harmful intent is already represented before refusal becomes decisive would rule out refusal-before-decode as the shared explanation, although it would not settle other causes of cipher jailbreaks. In the topic-substitution check, the generic goal of mechanistic LLM safety would not merit this score; the increment comes specifically from the predicted cross-layer ordering and its behavioral consequence.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is a “late-layer refusal re-check that reads the refusal direction from the later, post-decode layers,” an ex-ante inference-time intervention that can block a harmful answer after intent becomes legible but before it is emitted. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts more than where to look: successful cipher attacks should preserve the relation that decoding lags refusal commitment, so the ordering can serve as a diagnostic for whether this mitigation is needed. The asserted scope covers “Base64, ciphers, leetspeak” and potentially a general family of encoded jailbreaks, with downstream uptake by safety auditors and model deployers, though the claim’s own “model-dependent layer structure” limitation prevents treating it as architecture-invariant. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic interpretability for safety supplies neither this deployable re-check nor the transferable timing relation.
